item.name: 1 · Edge security (negative tests)
item.description: Proves the gateway's JWT validation, RBAC, internal-API blocking, input validation, and zero-trust re-validation in the services.

request.description: Gateway rejects unauthenticated calls.
Signature/format validation against Keycloak JWKS.
Coarse RBAC at the gateway: `POST /api/v1/trips` needs ROLE_RIDER.
`/api/v1/drivers/**` needs ROLE_DRIVER.
Even an ADMIN cannot reach service-to-service APIs through the public gateway (`denyAll`).

item.name: 1.6 Zero trust: trip-service rejects missing token → 401

request.description: Bypassing the gateway doesn't help: every downstream service validates the JWT itself.
`@DecimalMax("90")` on `GeoPoint.lat`. No trip is created.
The evaluator denies missing trips so ids cannot be probed.

item.name: 2 · Location service (CQRS command → Debezium → Redis read model)
item.description: Command side is called through the gateway; the query side (`/internal/**`) is called DIRECTLY on :8082 because the gateway blocks it. Each read request waits `propagation_delay_ms` (default 2 s) for Postgres → Debezium → Kafka → Redis.

item.name: 8 · Rate limiting (sliding window)
item.description: Route `trip-service` allows 20 requests / 10 s per user. Run request 8.1 with the COLLECTION RUNNER: 30 iterations, delay 0 ms. Expect ~20 responses without 429, then 429s until the window slides.

item.name: 8.1 Hammer a route (run 30× with no delay)

exec: pm.test('allowed (200/403) or throttled (429) — never a 5xx', function () { pm.expect([200,403,404,429]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 429) { pm.test('429 Too Many Requests', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(429); }); }

request.description: Watch the console: `X-RateLimit-Remaining` counts down 19 → 0, then the status flips to 429. Wait 10 s and it recovers (sliding window, no boundary burst).

item.name: 9 · Resilience (manual steps interleaved)
item.description: Demonstrates degradation and fail-closed behaviour when location-service is down. Requests named 🛑/▶ are MANUAL: stop or start the location-service process, then continue. Needs rider1 to have NO active trip.

item.name: 9.1 🛑 MANUAL: stop location-service now (Ctrl-C), then send this

request.description: Baseline: both breakers CLOSED.

exec: pm.test('HTTP 202 Accepted (saga continues asynchronously)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); });
pm.test('Location header points at the trip', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.include(t.tripId); });
pm.test('surge degraded to neutral 1.0 (fallback used)', function () { pm.expect(Number(pm.response.json().surgeMultiplier)).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Inserts trip + saga_instance + outbox(HOLD_PAYMENT) + outbox(TRIP_REQUESTED) in ONE DB transaction. Returns 202 because payment/matching continue in the background. **location-service is DOWN**: the surge lookup times out/fails and the fallback returns multiplier 1.0, so booking still succeeds (graceful degradation).

item.name: 10 · Gateway circuit breaker (manual)
item.description: Stop trip-service, then run the request below. The gateway's CircuitBreaker filter forwards to the fallback controller.

item.name: 10.1 🛑 MANUAL: stop trip-service, then GET a trip through the gateway → 503 + Retry-After

exec: pm.test('503 from gateway fallback', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(503); });

request.description: GET is retried twice by the gateway Retry filter, then the breaker/fallback answers. POSTs are never retried.
